headline: The hole in the rulebook: Lode Runner's trap finally catches someone
lede: Lode Runner-LITE documented that guards fall into your holes and get buried in deep shafts — but walkers were quietly blocked from pit mouths, so no hole had ever caught anyone outside a test scenario. This shift made the physics match the promise: dig, walk over the mouth and drop in, dig the shaft deeper from the bottom, and a guard you baited rides the upper hole when the five-second fuse closes.

notes.text: Two diggable strata: the vault floor's bottom row became diggable floor-rock, so a shaft can be two cells deep — the original's signature burial.

New laws, each mutant-proven: holes catch walkers (player AND guards — chasers route across pit mouths and fall in), pit-bottom Down deepens the shaft, Up clambers you out, and the burial arithmetic (two climbs vs one fuse) is pinned as a check in its own right.

The solver never digs, so every attract demo, ghost and WATCH route is byte-identical — 8/8 mutants die, lodeplay grades the whole dig-drop-deepen-climb chain with real keys, and the live prod bundle was verified carrying the new event.
Decorative-law lesson: when a README admits something is 'proven by scenario, not by play', it's a dead-rule alarm — drive the law end-to-end with the inputs a player actually has.
